North Florida plays to standstill against College of Charleston

Rachel Bacchus, Sports Reporter | Aug 30, 2026
Rachel Bacchus
The North Florida Ospreys tied against the College of Charleston Cougars with a final score, 1-1.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:48
Instaread

The University of North Florida Ospreys’ match against the College of Charleston Cougars ended in a draw on Aug. 27.

The match marks the women’s soccer team’s first tie against the Cougars. It also marks junior midfielder Morgan Guillemette’s first collegiate goal.

First half

The match started with the Cougars maintaining consistent control of the ball, earning three corner kicks in the first 15 minutes. The Ospreys made good use of the control they could get by making three shots on goal in the first 15 minutes. 

A total of 11 shots were made by both teams by the end of the first half. Despite both teams’ performance, neither was able to make a dent in the other’s defense. The first half ended with neither team scoring and the game tied 0-0.

Second half

Going into the second half, both teams continued to put up strong defenses with neither team budging. About 27 minutes into the second half, the Ospreys found their opening.

Amid increasing applause and rain, Guillemette scored her first collegiate goal on an assist from junior midfielder Brooke Susi. The Ospreys led 1-0 halfway through the second half.

The Ospreys fought to maintain their lead, but with three minutes left, Ospreys sophomore defender Skya Horth committed a foul, giving the College of Charleston a penalty kick.

Cougars senior forward Bella Antonio converted the penalty kick to tie the game at 1-1.

With neither team able to take the lead, the game ended in a draw.

The Ospreys travel to face the Alabama A&M Bulldogs on Sept. 3. Kickoff is at 4 p.m. at Bulldog Soccer Field in Huntsville, Ala.
